title: Explore the vocabulary
intro: You can't query a dataset without knowing its vocabulary, so start by asking BeingDB what it contains.
Facts are written as **predicates**: a name applied to some arguments. For example, the dataset contains the fact:
The predicate is `created_by`, and it has two arguments. We write this as `created_by/2`; the number after the slash is the **arity**, the number of arguments.
The list below comes straight from the loaded data. Filter it, and click a predicate to see more about it.

notes: These predicates appear throughout the tutorial:

head: Predicate
Meaning
rows: An artist who is the subject of an interview
A work and who made it
A work or an artist's practice uses a medium

notes: Notice roles like `WorkOrArtist`: some predicates mix kinds of entity in one position. A later lesson shows how to deal with that.
try: Filter for `year` to see every predicate that records a year.
